matrix: For build 17 the 26 behavioural probes of the method were also run through Claude Code in seven arms of delivery: no ACR text, the card and the kernel as system text, the card pasted, the card as stored instructions, and each plugin (570 conversations, two models of one provider). The screens of the probes are text patterns, the replies they flagged were read by the party that wrote them, most cells hold one or two runs, and the container loaded tools of its own into every session. It shows that each way of delivering the method works as a program and where the ways differ. It supports no rate and no conclusion about effect. For build 18 the conversation in which an assistant had recorded a refutation that rested on its own written derivation was held again, with and without permission to run a command, and further conversations exercised the host's observation of checks; the release record lists them. They are uncontrolled sessions of the same kind, a handful, and support no rate. For build 19 twelve further conversations of the same kind were held on the final archives: the earlier ones again, one in which a command was run before the review and then offered as its check, which the host refused, and two on a claim the reviewed text disclaims. The probes were not run again on build 19. For build 20 nine further conversations of the same kind were held on 13 November, on plugin folders that are the same bytes as those delivered: five of the earlier ones again; one in which the command fails, so that what is recorded is the host's report of a failure; and two in which the assistant is asked to record, as material it was given, a file it writes during the review. In the first of those two the provider stopped the opening turn before the model replied, and the file was not permitted to be written; in the second the file was recorded as PRODUCED and a refutation resting on it was refused, and the provider withheld the model's closing reply. A file written in the very second of commissioning cannot be arranged in a conversation and was not tried in one. The figure of 441 sessions is carried forward from build 19 and was not recounted; build 20 adds 19. The probes were not run again on build 20. Build 21 held no further sessions of that kind: its sessions are the Calibration in item 6. In the probe runs of builds 16 to 19 an assistant could read any file of the machine that held the packet, the probes and their criteria, because the host's read-only file tools ask no permission; that was not known then, and those runs are weaker than they were described to be.
calibration:
Two Calibrations (Core Section 14.4) have been taken, both on 13 November 2026, of five ways of delivering ACR to two models of one provider in Claude Code: no ACR text, the card, the kernel, the `pcp` plugin and the `pcp-os` plugin. The first, of build 21, is withdrawn for the two plugins; the second, of this build, replaces it.

   **What was wrong with the first.** To keep the probes and their criteria from the assistants measured, it confined each assistant's file tools. That also kept the two plugins from their own files. Of the 75 `pcp-os` conversations that began a review, 71 said that a file could not be read or that no review could be commissioned; of the 87 with `pcp`, 23 said a file could not be read. Its counts for the plugins describe an arrangement nobody uses. Two criteria were applied where their setting did not hold, one counted against an assistant a question that the Core permits, and every conversation had one reader, whose readings were in places wrong. Its statement that the plugins made the smaller model fail a control was also wrong in its cause: see below.

   **The second.** The same thresholds, fixed before the run: retrieval for at least 0.9 with nothing invented, application passed at least 0.8, every control passed. Retrieval: 44 questions to each configuration, scored by the packet's tool. Application: the 26 probes twice each, 520 conversations, each read against its criterion by another model that was not told the configuration, and read a second time by a third. The assistants' tools were not confined: each session ran where the probes, their criteria and the run's own files were not on the disk it could see, and a search of that disk as the session saw it, before and after, found none of them. No session had a shell or a write tool.

   | Delivery | Smaller model: retrieval, application | Larger model: retrieval, application |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | No ACR text | 44 of 44, 40 of 52 | 44 of 44, 37 of 52 |
   | Card | 44 of 44, 43 of 52 | 44 of 44, 44 of 52 |
   | Kernel | 44 of 44, 45 of 52 | 39 of 44, 49 of 52 |
   | `pcp` plugin | 42 of 44, 48 of 52 | 44 of 44, 47 of 52 |
   | `pcp-os` plugin | 44 of 44, 45 of 52 | 18 of 44, 50 of 52 |

   Nothing was invented in any configuration. Four of the ten configurations met every threshold: the card with both models, the kernel with the smaller and the `pcp` plugin with the larger. Six did not, and by the rule fixed beforehand the statement that the delivery onboards the model is refuted for them in this scope. The reasons differ. With no ACR text the models passed 40 and 37 of 52, below the threshold: most probes ask for conduct these models show anyway, and the most any delivery added was 8 conversations of 52 with the smaller model and 13 with the larger. The kernel with the larger model failed on retrieval, as it did in the first Calibration (39 of 44). The `pcp-os` plugin with the larger model passed 50 of 52 conversations and failed on retrieval, 18 of 44: one of its two replies held two lists, the second a correction of the first, and the scoring tool, which takes one list, scored none of its 22 answers; scored apart, for information only, the two lists give 20 and 21 of 22. The other reply had 18 of 22. With the smaller model each plugin failed a control in which nobody asks for ACR, a sentence with one misspelt word to correct (3 of 4 and 2 of 4 passed).

   **That control fails because of the host's tools, not the plugins.** Afterwards the same sentence was put to the smaller model twelve times in each of four arrangements. With no tools it returned exactly the corrected sentence 12 times of 12. With the host's file tools and no plugin, 5 of 12. With `pcp`, 4 of 12; with `pcp-os`, 2 of 12. The arms that are text only are measured without tools, so this control compares arrangements that differ in more than the delivery. Twelve runs support no difference between 5, 4 and 2.

   Limits. One party wrote the probes, the criteria, the thresholds and the harness, ran it, and changed four criteria and both plugins after reading the first run, so a count that is higher than the first's may be owed to that reading. Both readers are models of the same provider as the subjects; they agreed on 474 of the 520 conversations, the count is the first reader's, and the 46 in dispute are listed in the record and were not settled by a person. Two runs of a probe support no rate. One file of the `pcp-os` plugin as delivered differs from the plugin measured: the body of its skill about PCP OS itself, which was found to be out of date and corrected while the run was under way; no measured conversation loaded that skill. A Calibration measures onboarding and nothing else: it is not evidence that ACR improves any work.

   The maker's own entry. The assistant that made this build was given the 26 probes of the fourteenth round one turn at a time in its own session, without their identifiers or criteria, by a program it had written; its replies were read by two other models. Retrieval 22 of 22; application 25 of 26, the two readers disagreeing on the one. The Claim that it is onboarded is recorded CONDITIONAL, not supported: it administered its own measurement, and it had read a description of eight of the items.
